## Details

### Update: 5 May 2026

Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.

### Update: 19 December 2025

These tables were revised to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for one area in the North East. This impacts 2023 data only, which has now been corrected in this version.

These statistics include the following estimates at the region and local authority levels in Great Britain, for domestic, non-domestic and total gas consumption:

*   number of gas meters
*   total consumption
*   mean and median consumption per meter

The subnational gas consumption statistics gained National Statistics status in March 2008.

## Details

### Update: 5 May 2026

Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.

### Update: 19 December 2025

These tables were revised to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for one area in the North East. This impacts 2023 data only, which has now been corrected in this version.

These statistics include the following estimates at the region and local authority levels in Great Britain, for domestic, non-domestic and total gas consumption:

*   number of gas meters
*   total consumption
*   mean and median consumption per meter

The subnational gas consumption statistics gained National Statistics status in March 2008.

# Sheet 1: _Cover sheet_
**Subnational gas consumption, Great Britain, 2005 - 2024**![Image 1](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69f9bf208f3213f7384ecae6/9e1ae32f-ea6d-47f0-9f72-206e207ec509_html_574153dcb953ba7c.png)
This workbook presents Accredited Official Statistics on gas consumption by country, region and local authority in Great Britain. These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.
A non-weather corrected version of these statistics is also published for the years 2015 and 2024 and can be found at:
[Regional and local authority gas consumption statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/gas-sales-and-numbers-of-customers-by-region-and-local-authority)
The gas consumption years used in these statistics are as follows:
Prior to 2014: same October – September period as 2014 and 2015
2014: October 2013 – September 2014
2015: October 2014 – September 2015
2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
2019: mid-May 2019 – mid-May 2020
2020: mid-May 2020 – mid-May 2021
2021: mid-May 2021 – mid-May 2022
2022: mid-May 2022 – mid-May 2023
2023: mid-May 2023 – mid-May 2024
2024: mid-May 2024 – mid-May 2025
**Contents**
Following this Cover sheet there is a Notes sheet containing a table of notes which accompany the data tables. This is followed by the gas consumption estimates which are presented in the form of one sheet for each of the years 2005 - 2024.
**Publication dates**
Publication date: 18 December 2025
Next update: December 2026
**Revisions**
The statistics for the years 2015 onwards are revised each year to reflect additional/new information acquired. This includes:
- Updates to the National Statistics Postcodes Lookup (NSPL), which is used to match postcodes to local authorities. These updates reflect changes to   
 postcodes and local authorities. The latest version of the NSPL is used for each year for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Updates to the meter address information resulting in corrections and updates to postcodes. The most recent valid postcode information for each meter   
 is used across all years for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Additional information gathered about earlier years, from investigating anomalous year-on-year changes in consumption.
The 2023 table was revised on 19th December to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for 1 area in the North East.
Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised on 5th May 2026 to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.
**Methodology**
These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data provided by Xoserve (who compile meter level data from gas shippers, who in turn receive the data from gas suppliers). Xoserve provide annualised estimates of consumption (AQs) for all gas meters. Xoserve provide the AQs on a weather corrected basis by a process which accounts for regional temperatures and wind speed and incorporates trends.
The gas meters are classified as being domestic or non-domestic according to their (weather-corrected) gas consumption. Those with an annual consumption less than the industry cut-off of 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic and the rest are classified as non-domestic. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.
The Number of meters columns only includes consuming meters (meters which have consumed gas in the given year), with non-consuming meters reported in a separate column from 2015 onwards. Both mean and median consumption statistics are based on consuming meters only.
For more information about these gas consumption statistics, see Section 2 of:
[Subnational energy statistics methodology note](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/regional-energy-data-guidance-note)
**Units**
The figures for average (mean and median) gas consumption per meter point are presented in kilowatt hours (kWh).
The figures for total gas consumption are presented in gigawatt hours (GWh). 1GWh = 1 million kWh.
Elsewhere, energy statistics are often presented in kilotonnes of oil equivalent (ktoe). 1 ktoe = 11.63 GWh.
Where no value is provided for mean/median consumption this is because there are no gas meters of the given type for the local authority in question.

# Sheet 1: _Cover sheet_
**Subnational gas consumption, Great Britain, 2005 - 2024**![Image 1](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69f9bf208f3213f7384ecae6/9e1ae32f-ea6d-47f0-9f72-206e207ec509_html_574153dcb953ba7c.png)
This workbook presents Accredited Official Statistics on gas consumption by country, region and local authority in Great Britain. These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.
A non-weather corrected version of these statistics is also published for the years 2015 and 2024 and can be found at:
[Regional and local authority gas consumption statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/gas-sales-and-numbers-of-customers-by-region-and-local-authority)
The gas consumption years used in these statistics are as follows:
Prior to 2014: same October – September period as 2014 and 2015
2014: October 2013 – September 2014
2015: October 2014 – September 2015
2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
2019: mid-May 2019 – mid-May 2020
2020: mid-May 2020 – mid-May 2021
2021: mid-May 2021 – mid-May 2022
2022: mid-May 2022 – mid-May 2023
2023: mid-May 2023 – mid-May 2024
2024: mid-May 2024 – mid-May 2025
**Contents**
Following this Cover sheet there is a Notes sheet containing a table of notes which accompany the data tables. This is followed by the gas consumption estimates which are presented in the form of one sheet for each of the years 2005 - 2024.
**Publication dates**
Publication date: 18 December 2025
Next update: December 2026
**Revisions**
The statistics for the years 2015 onwards are revised each year to reflect additional/new information acquired. This includes:
- Updates to the National Statistics Postcodes Lookup (NSPL), which is used to match postcodes to local authorities. These updates reflect changes to   
 postcodes and local authorities. The latest version of the NSPL is used for each year for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Updates to the meter address information resulting in corrections and updates to postcodes. The most recent valid postcode information for each meter   
 is used across all years for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Additional information gathered about earlier years, from investigating anomalous year-on-year changes in consumption.
The 2023 table was revised on 19th December to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for 1 area in the North East.
Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised on 5th May 2026 to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.
**Methodology**
These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data provided by Xoserve (who compile meter level data from gas shippers, who in turn receive the data from gas suppliers). Xoserve provide annualised estimates of consumption (AQs) for all gas meters. Xoserve provide the AQs on a weather corrected basis by a process which accounts for regional temperatures and wind speed and incorporates trends.
The gas meters are classified as being domestic or non-domestic according to their (weather-corrected) gas consumption. Those with an annual consumption less than the industry cut-off of 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic and the rest are classified as non-domestic. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.
The Number of meters columns only includes consuming meters (meters which have consumed gas in the given year), with non-consuming meters reported in a separate column from 2015 onwards. Both mean and median consumption statistics are based on consuming meters only.
For more information about these gas consumption statistics, see Section 2 of:
[Subnational energy statistics methodology note](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/regional-energy-data-guidance-note)
**Units**
The figures for average (mean and median) gas consumption per meter point are presented in kilowatt hours (kWh).
The figures for total gas consumption are presented in gigawatt hours (GWh). 1GWh = 1 million kWh.
Elsewhere, energy statistics are often presented in kilotonnes of oil equivalent (ktoe). 1 ktoe = 11.63 GWh.
Where no value is provided for mean/median consumption this is because there are no gas meters of the given type for the local authority in question.

**Subnational gas consumption, Great Britain, 2005 - 2024**![Image 1](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69f9bf208f3213f7384ecae6/9e1ae32f-ea6d-47f0-9f72-206e207ec509_html_574153dcb953ba7c.png)
This workbook presents Accredited Official Statistics on gas consumption by country, region and local authority in Great Britain. These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.
A non-weather corrected version of these statistics is also published for the years 2015 and 2024 and can be found at:
[Regional and local authority gas consumption statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/gas-sales-and-numbers-of-customers-by-region-and-local-authority)
The gas consumption years used in these statistics are as follows:
Prior to 2014: same October – September period as 2014 and 2015
2014: October 2013 – September 2014
2015: October 2014 – September 2015
2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
2019: mid-May 2019 – mid-May 2020
2020: mid-May 2020 – mid-May 2021
2021: mid-May 2021 – mid-May 2022
2022: mid-May 2022 – mid-May 2023
2023: mid-May 2023 – mid-May 2024
2024: mid-May 2024 – mid-May 2025
**Contents**
Following this Cover sheet there is a Notes sheet containing a table of notes which accompany the data tables. This is followed by the gas consumption estimates which are presented in the form of one sheet for each of the years 2005 - 2024.
**Publication dates**
Publication date: 18 December 2025
Next update: December 2026
**Revisions**
The statistics for the years 2015 onwards are revised each year to reflect additional/new information acquired. This includes:
- Updates to the National Statistics Postcodes Lookup (NSPL), which is used to match postcodes to local authorities. These updates reflect changes to   
 postcodes and local authorities. The latest version of the NSPL is used for each year for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Updates to the meter address information resulting in corrections and updates to postcodes. The most recent valid postcode information for each meter   
 is used across all years for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Additional information gathered about earlier years, from investigating anomalous year-on-year changes in consumption.
The 2023 table was revised on 19th December to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for 1 area in the North East.
Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised on 5th May 2026 to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.
**Methodology**
These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data provided by Xoserve (who compile meter level data from gas shippers, who in turn receive the data from gas suppliers). Xoserve provide annualised estimates of consumption (AQs) for all gas meters. Xoserve provide the AQs on a weather corrected basis by a process which accounts for regional temperatures and wind speed and incorporates trends.
The gas meters are classified as being domestic or non-domestic according to their (weather-corrected) gas consumption. Those with an annual consumption less than the industry cut-off of 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic and the rest are classified as non-domestic. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.
The Number of meters columns only includes consuming meters (meters which have consumed gas in the given year), with non-consuming meters reported in a separate column from 2015 onwards. Both mean and median consumption statistics are based on consuming meters only.
For more information about these gas consumption statistics, see Section 2 of:
[Subnational energy statistics methodology note](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/regional-energy-data-guidance-note)
**Units**
The figures for average (mean and median) gas consumption per meter point are presented in kilowatt hours (kWh).
The figures for total gas consumption are presented in gigawatt hours (GWh). 1GWh = 1 million kWh.
Elsewhere, energy statistics are often presented in kilotonnes of oil equivalent (ktoe). 1 ktoe = 11.63 GWh.
Where no value is provided for mean/median consumption this is because there are no gas meters of the given type for the local authority in question.

# Sheet 1: _Cover sheet_
**Subnational gas consumption, Great Britain, 2005 - 2024**![Image 1](https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69f9bf208f3213f7384ecae6/9e1ae32f-ea6d-47f0-9f72-206e207ec509_html_574153dcb953ba7c.png)
This workbook presents Accredited Official Statistics on gas consumption by country, region and local authority in Great Britain. These estimates are weather-corrected. This means that the effect of differences in weather conditions between years has been removed to provide more like for like comparisons over time.
A non-weather corrected version of these statistics is also published for the years 2015 and 2024 and can be found at:
[Regional and local authority gas consumption statistics](https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/gas-sales-and-numbers-of-customers-by-region-and-local-authority)
The gas consumption years used in these statistics are as follows:
Prior to 2014: same October – September period as 2014 and 2015
2014: October 2013 – September 2014
2015: October 2014 – September 2015
2016: mid-July 2016 – mid-July 2017
2017: mid-June 2017 – mid-June 2018
2018: mid-May 2018 – mid-May 2019
2019: mid-May 2019 – mid-May 2020
2020: mid-May 2020 – mid-May 2021
2021: mid-May 2021 – mid-May 2022
2022: mid-May 2022 – mid-May 2023
2023: mid-May 2023 – mid-May 2024
2024: mid-May 2024 – mid-May 2025
**Contents**
Following this Cover sheet there is a Notes sheet containing a table of notes which accompany the data tables. This is followed by the gas consumption estimates which are presented in the form of one sheet for each of the years 2005 - 2024.
**Publication dates**
Publication date: 18 December 2025
Next update: December 2026
**Revisions**
The statistics for the years 2015 onwards are revised each year to reflect additional/new information acquired. This includes:
- Updates to the National Statistics Postcodes Lookup (NSPL), which is used to match postcodes to local authorities. These updates reflect changes to   
 postcodes and local authorities. The latest version of the NSPL is used for each year for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Updates to the meter address information resulting in corrections and updates to postcodes. The most recent valid postcode information for each meter   
 is used across all years for 2015 onwards for consistency across the time series.
- Additional information gathered about earlier years, from investigating anomalous year-on-year changes in consumption.
The 2023 table was revised on 19th December to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for 1 area in the North East.
Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised on 5th May 2026 to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.
**Methodology**
These figures are based on meter level gas consumption data provided by Xoserve (who compile meter level data from gas shippers, who in turn receive the data from gas suppliers). Xoserve provide annualised estimates of consumption (AQs) for all gas meters. Xoserve provide the AQs on a weather corrected basis by a process which accounts for regional temperatures and wind speed and incorporates trends.
The gas meters are classified as being domestic or non-domestic according to their (weather-corrected) gas consumption. Those with an annual consumption less than the industry cut-off of 73,200 kWh are classified as domestic and the rest are classified as non-domestic. This means that some small industrial and commercial consumers will be classified as domestic.
The Number of meters columns only includes consuming meters (meters which have consumed gas in the given year), with non-consuming meters reported in a separate column from 2015 onwards. Both mean and median consumption statistics are based on consuming meters only.
For more information about these gas consumption statistics, see Section 2 of:
[Subnational energy statistics methodology note](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/regional-energy-data-guidance-note)
**Units**
The figures for average (mean and median) gas consumption per meter point are presented in kilowatt hours (kWh).
The figures for total gas consumption are presented in gigawatt hours (GWh). 1GWh = 1 million kWh.
Elsewhere, energy statistics are often presented in kilotonnes of oil equivalent (ktoe). 1 ktoe = 11.63 GWh.
Where no value is provided for mean/median consumption this is because there are no gas meters of the given type for the local authority in question.

# Stacked gas consumption statistics data

Gas consumption data for 2005 to 2024 as a single table, with years stacked one above the other.

From:[Department for Energy Security and Net Zero](https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/department-for-energy-security-and-net-zero)Published:20 December 2018 Last updated: 5 May 2026 — See all updates

### Update: 5 May 2026

Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.

### Update: 19 December 2025

These tables were revised to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for one area in the North East. This impacts 2023 data only, which has now been corrected in this version.

These tables provide the gas time series data from 2005 to 2024 in csv format. This is aimed at analytical users of sub-national data.

The cover sheets in the [Excel versions of these data](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sub-national-gas-consumption-data) provide guidance on using the data.

# Stacked gas consumption statistics data

Gas consumption data for 2005 to 2024 as a single table, with years stacked one above the other.

From:[Department for Energy Security and Net Zero](https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/department-for-energy-security-and-net-zero)Published:20 December 2018 Last updated: 5 May 2026 — See all updates

### Update: 5 May 2026

Tables for 2005 to 2013 were revised to correct for a processing error identified for some Local Authorities in Wales which had resulted in data being shown against incorrect Local Authorities. Total figures for Wales were not impacted.

### Update: 19 December 2025

These tables were revised to correct an error in the non-domestic gas consumption for one area in the North East. This impacts 2023 data only, which has now been corrected in this version.

These tables provide the gas time series data from 2005 to 2024 in csv format. This is aimed at analytical users of sub-national data.

The cover sheets in the [Excel versions of these data](https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sub-national-gas-consumption-data) provide guidance on using the data.

steps.text:
I began by locating the ONS “Subnational gas consumption statistics” dataset, which contains domestic‑gas consumption figures for every local authority from 2005 – 2024. The dataset is hosted on the GOV.UK publishing service and is available both as an Excel file and as a single‑sheet CSV file (URL: <https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/69f9c094a40aa2232fede4af/gas_LA_stacked_2005-2024.csv>).

When I fetched the CSV, the tool returned only a short excerpt that included the 2005 values for the five unitary authorities in the question (Flintshire, County Durham, Bedford, North Lincolnshire and Telford & Wrekin). The excerpt did not contain any rows for 2012 or 2023, and the tool did not provide a way to retrieve the remainder of the file.

Because the 2012 and 2023 domestic‑gas consumption values (in GWh) for each of those authorities are not available in the data that I was able to download, I cannot calculate the change in consumption between 2012 and 2023, and therefore I cannot identify which authority had the largest drop.

I was unable to locate an alternative source or a more comprehensive download of the ONS dataset that includes the required years. If you have access to the full CSV/Excel file or another ONS resource that contains the 2012–2023 domestic‑gas consumption figures for these unitary authorities, please share it and I can proceed with the calculation.
